documentation.rationale: VIN, title status, and a Carfax accident/owner summary are present (identity/terms half), but none of the five model-critical maintenance items — coolant pipes, transfer case/driveshaft, air suspension, fault scan, smog readiness — has an invoice, photo, or report behind it; the '20 service records' figure is cited but not itemized.

condition.rationale: No mechanical fault is disclosed and the underbody/engine-bay photos look tidy, but every major 955 Turbo failure point remains entirely unverified despite the seller being asked directly and declining to inspect further; the lift-kit conversion adds unknowns to the air suspension specifically, and a torn rooftop tent is the one disclosed defect.

price_value.rationale: Current bid of $11,251 sits within the broad $8k-$16k range for 'unsorted' 955 Turbos per market notes, but the total absence of documentation for the big-ticket items plus a heavy off-road conversion (which narrows resale per market notes) means the price does not yet reflect the likely $4k-$8k+ catch-up risk.

mission_fit.rationale: Genuine off-road/overland capability (low-range transfer case, lift, rooftop tent, skid plate) meaningfully differs from the RX 350's on-road utility, satisfying the branch's requirement to justify itself by capability the household SUV doesn't already provide.

logistics.rationale: Sheridan, WY is a significant distance from Carmel, CA, but the seller has offered PPI access at any local shop at buyer expense, making inspection-before-purchase feasible with coordination and transport cost.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A desirable factory spec (PASM, Bose, heated seats) in an attractive color plus a distinctive, character-rich overland build is offset by the heavy off-road modification, which per the buyer's stated preference for stock/mostly-stock condition is at best a modest positive and narrows the buyer pool.

evidence.mission_note: This Cayenne Turbo offers real capability differentiation from the RX 350 — 4WD low-range, lift, and rooftop-tent camping platform for Highway 1, Sierra, and Big Sur use — but as a 20-year-old modified 955 Turbo with every major documented-failure point unverified, it reads as a discretionary capability purchase rather than a dependable bridge for the 335i's unreliability.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a low-mileage (47k), clean-titled, accident-free-per-Carfax 2004 Cayenne Turbo with an extensive dealer-installed overland conversion (lift kit, bumper, rack, tent, skid plate) and a VIN that matches decode with no contradictions. Against the model's known weak points, the seller directly states in the comment thread that the plastic coolant crossover pipes have never been scoped or replaced, and no invoice, photo, leak-down test, or all-module scan is offered for the coolant system, transfer case, driveshaft, or air suspension despite multiple specific buyer requests. Carfax reports 20 service entries and at least one open recall, but neither the service line items nor the recall completion status are itemized in the listing, and VIN history shows the open recalls include a transfer-case oil-pump directional fault and a fuel-pump flange crack campaign. A referenced October 2025 PPI is mentioned by a commenter but its report is not produced by the seller. Photos show a clean engine bay and underbody and a torn rooftop-tent panel, the only disclosed physical defect. The seller is responsive and offers PPI access at a Sheridan, WY shop at buyer expense, but no inspection has actually occurred, and one commenter's suspicion of exhaust modification went unanswered.
evidence.next_action: Arrange and complete an independent PPI in Sheridan, WY (borescope of the coolant pipes, transfer case/driveline check, air-suspension leak-down, and full module fault scan) and obtain the referenced October 2025 PPI report and recall-completion documentation before bidding further or transacting.
